chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Ali ibn Suleiman, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah al-Hashemi, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abil Balad, (on the authority of his father,) on the authority of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had two rings. On one of them it was written: 'There is no God but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God,' and on the other it was written: 'God speaks the truth.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no God but God (Shahada)
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: Muhammad is the Messenger of God

ai.seo_question: What were the inscriptions on the two rings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records in *Al-Khisal* that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) wore two distinct rings: one inscribed with the Shahada ('La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah') and the other with 'Sadaqa Allah' (God spoke the truth). This narration underscores the significance of the Prophet's personal adornments as symbols of divine truth and prophetic authority, a detail often discussed in Shia hadith literature regarding the physical manifestations of his status.
